Houston, Alonzo Bodden’s latest special, *How Do You Spell Moth?*, is worth knowing before he gets here.

He won NBC’s third season of *Last Comic Standing* and has been telling the truth onstage since 1993. His sets move from current events to everyday dumb questions, with a calm, sharp point of view. I’d go for the conversation he builds with the room.

Punch Line Houston · Thursday, November 5, 2026

Houston, you may know Desi Banks as Fonk the Freak on Sherman’s Showcase.

Onstage, he turns family, fatherhood, and everyday Southern life into stories that feel familiar. He started with online character sketches, but live stand-up gives him room to tell the whole truth. I’d catch him now, especially if your group has that one cousin who makes every dinner a show.

Houston Improv · Friday, November 6, 2026

Houston, Nikki Glaser hosted the 2026 Golden Globes. Now she’s bringing her no-filter stand-up to Sugar Land.

Her Hulu special, *Good Girl*, arrived this year. Live, she gets candid about dating, sobriety, insecurities, and the awkward parts of growing up. Go for the tight roast-style punchlines. Stay for the honesty.

Houston, Karen Morgan released her 2026 Dry Bar Comedy special, *Put Some Butter On It.*

If you like comedy about family, aging, and the odd gap between generations, bring your people. Morgan grew up in Athens, Georgia, and her stand-up has a clean, Southern, story-first feel. She also performed on *The Talk* in 2024. I’d see her live for the kind of set different generations can enjoy together.

The Riot Comedy Club — Conroe · Friday, November 6, 2026

Houston, Ramiro González was on Escuela de Nada in March, talking about the reality of Cuba in 2026.

He grew up on Cuba’s Isla de la Juventud and began doing stand-up in Uruguay in 2019. His Spanish-language set makes room for Cuba, moving away, and learning a new culture—while keeping the room in the conversation. I’d go for the stories and the way he brings people in.

Punch Line Houston · Friday, November 6, 2026
